table_rule: Every useful printed table is transcribed cell-by-cell, checked against current authoritative data, then rebuilt as semantic responsive HTML. Printed and corrected values are both retained where the change itself has exam value.

verified_groups.result: MHA confirms total land border 15,106.7 km and country-wise lengths: Bangladesh 4,096.70; China 3,488; Pakistan 3,323; Nepal 1,751; Myanmar 1,643; Bhutan 699; Afghanistan 106 km. Current UT wording must replace the book's older Jammu and Kashmir state wording.
MHA now states 11,098.81 km including island territories. The older 7,516.6 km series will be retained only as a clearly dated former measurement, not mixed into the revised state ranking table.
CSIR-NPL confirms Indian Standard Time is maintained by CSIR-NPL and equals UTC+05:30. Longitude and Mirzapur-location claims still require separate official cartographic verification.

Official AP district portals confirm Markapuram District was operational from 31 December 2025 and provide a gazette order. The Polavaram portal confirms a functioning newly formed district site, but its generic page contains internally unreliable copied geography text; district counts, composition and regional grouping require gazette/map-level verification before scoring.

India Code confirms 12 nautical miles for territorial waters and sovereignty over water, seabed, subsoil and airspace, subject to innocent passage. UNCLOS confirms the 24 nautical mile outer limit for the contiguous zone, 200 nautical mile EEZ limit, and a distinct seabed/subsoil continental-shelf regime that may extend beyond 200 nautical miles when Article 76 criteria are met.

MEA records confirm the 1974 LBA, 2011 Protocol, exchange of ratification instruments on 6 June 2015, transfer at midnight on 31 July 2015, and the 111 Indian-enclave to 51 Bangladeshi-enclave directions.

APSAC gives 12°33′–19°09′ N, 76°38′–84°42′ E and 162,970 km² in a dated 2018 state dataset; these differ slightly from the book's coordinate rounding and must be source-labelled. The Alluri Sitharama Raju district administration confirms reorganisation from 13 to 26 districts on 4 April 2022 and from 26 to 28 with effect from 31 December 2025. Markapuram's official portal confirms its formation and current district profile.

NCERT's 2025-26 India—Size and Location chapter confirms mainland latitude 8°4′ N–37°6′ N, longitude 68°7′ E–97°25′ E, Tropic of Cancer 23°30′ N, roughly two hours of east–west local-time difference, 82°30′ E through Mirzapur as the standard meridian, 28 states and 8 UTs, the principal land neighbours, and Sri Lanka/Maldives as southern island neighbours. Survey of India supplies the current authoritative political map.

The Census of India Population Finder identifies 2011 figures as Primary Census Abstract data and provides a separate population-projections route. Notes and MCQs must label census counts and projections separately with year and territorial coverage.

MEA's Simla Agreement text confirms that the Line of Control in Jammu and Kashmir resulted from the ceasefire of 17 December 1971 and must be respected without prejudice to either side's recognised position. A Government of India parliamentary answer confirms that the India–China Line of Actual Control is not commonly delineated and that the two sides have differing perceptions in some areas. These sources support treating LoC and LAC as distinct control-line contexts, not internationally demarcated boundaries. AGPL remains a separate Siachen deployment term and requires its own primary-source verification before all associated details are scored.

The SAARC Secretariat confirms that the Charter was signed at Dhaka on 8 December 1985 and lists eight member states. Its official compilation reproduces the Joint Declaration admitting Afghanistan as a member from 3 April 2007.
MEA treaty records confirm the 1949 friendship treaty and the updated treaty signed on 8 February 2007, which entered into force after exchange of ratification instruments on 2 March 2007.

The constitutional text supports India and Bharat as the formal Article 1 names. IGNCA-hosted historical material supports the Indus/Sindhu linguistic pathway for India and the Persian historical use of Hindustan. Traditional literary labels such as Jambudvipa remain contextual cosmographical terms and are not mapped as modern political divisions; the notes deliberately avoid presenting one disputed origin story for Bharat as settled fact.

MEA's 30 June 2017 statement confirms the Doklam road-construction episode, Bhutan's protest, India–Bhutan consultation, the tri-junction context and India's stated security concern. The geographical linkage to the Siliguri Corridor is retained as map interpretation; variable corridor-width figures remain source-location dependent.

Shipping Ministry annual reports describe the proposed channel linking the Gulf of Mannar and Bay of Bengal through shallow waters, the stoppage of work after litigation, environmental evaluation and later exploration of an alignment that would avoid damaging Adam's Bridge/Rama Setu. Route-specific distance and time savings are therefore not treated as universal values.

PIB/Ministry of Defence confirms that Operation Meghdoot began on 13 April 1984 to secure strategic heights in the Siachen–Saltoro sector. PIB's Kargil account confirms infiltration across the LoC in 1999 and Operation Vijay to evict the intruders. Glacier-length superlatives and current LoC-adjoining district lists remain excluded from scoring pending a defined cartographic source.

MEA's foreign-relations record describes Sir Creek as a 96-km strip of water in the Rann of Kutch marshlands and records a joint survey undertaken in 2007 in the context of the India–Pakistan land boundary and international maritime-boundary delimitation. The competing legal alignment interpretations remain described rather than independently scored.

The Ministry of Defence release confirms that Operation Sindoor began on 7 May 2025 after the Pahalgam attack and initially targeted nine terrorist-infrastructure sites in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir. The notes distinguish it from the 2016 surgical strikes and the 2019 Balakot air strike.

MEA's treaty record confirms the 1950 Treaty of Peace and Friendship. Kalapani–Lipulekh and Susta remain described neutrally as boundary-disagreement contexts; the treaty itself is not presented as resolving those separate questions.

A 2018 MHA parliamentary reply corrects the book's broad wording: the boundary was settled under the 1967 agreement, while ground demarcation involving nine boundary pillars in the Manipur sector remained incomplete.

The Maldives government partner resource describes 22 natural atolls, some 1,190 islands and average island elevation no more than about two metres above sea level, supporting the low-elevation vulnerability explanation.

Survey of India's re-verified series gives a national coastline of 11,098.81 km and a single comparable state-wise table. It places Gujarat first, Tamil Nadu second and Andhra Pradesh third among states. The notes warn against mixing these values with the older 7,516.6-km series.

NCERT confirms the Tropic of Cancer at 23°30′ N and its near-bisection of India; its official map/exercise confirms Rajasthan, Chhattisgarh and Tripura as crossed states and Odisha as not crossed. The standard west-to-east eight-state sequence is retained as map reading. City, river and protected-area claims are not treated as exact line intersections without coordinates or GIS evidence; those rows remain explicitly unscored map practice.

NCERT confirms India’s approximately 3.28 million km² area, 2.4% world share and seventh-place textbook convention. Census of India’s Administrative Atlas demonstrates why district counts require a reference date: its 2011 atlas describes the setup as of 31 December 2010 and records 640 districts then. Consequently changing largest/smallest district and state-by-district-count rows remain dated comparison guidance, not current scored facts.

MHA confirms the 31 October 2019 creation of the Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh Union Territories and the 26 January 2020 merger creating Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu. Survey of India’s current political-map service is the controlling cartographic reference for state adjacency. The notes correctly separate neighbouring states from adjoining Union Territories; changing district-level counts are not inferred from this table.

MHA’s border-management record confirms the international-border countries, lengths and adjoining Indian units. MEA’s Simla Agreement and a Government of India reply support the distinction between the India–Pakistan Line of Control and the India–China Line of Actual Control. MHA’s 2021 parliamentary reply confirms that inter-state boundary disputes are claims/demarcation issues and specifically lists Andhra Pradesh–Odisha. Variable local widths, current troop positions and unresolved alignments remain descriptive or unscored rather than guessed.

MEA’s 1976 treaty confirms the India–Sri Lanka maritime boundary in the Gulf of Mannar and Bay of Bengal, recalls the 1974 Palk Strait settlement, and records the India–Sri Lanka–Maldives trijunction. MEA’s Maldives brief confirms Maldives near Minicoy and the strategic 8° N channel context. The notes therefore retain Sri Lanka and Maldives as maritime neighbours while treating broad lists of every country facing an Indian sea as geographical context rather than a single legal category.

The Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act provides the legal bifurcation framework. Official Alluri Sitharama Raju and Markapuram district portals confirm the 13→26 transition on 4 April 2022 and 26→28 transition effective 31 December 2025. MHA confirms an Andhra Pradesh–Odisha boundary dispute and pending Andhra Pradesh–Telangana asset matters. The five state-level neighbours are retained; individual post-2025 border-district rows and statewide counts below district level remain book snapshots unless a single dated official political map/directory supports them. Notes now label those rows unscored instead of implying current verification.

unresolved_unscored_items: Exact Tropic-of-Cancer intersections with named cities, rivers and protected-area boundaries require coordinate/GIS evidence; the printed map-practice rows are not scored.
Current largest/smallest district and state-by-district-count rankings require a single dated nationwide administrative directory.
Variable local widths, live troop positions and unresolved boundary alignments are not converted into timeless scored facts.
Post-31-December-2025 Andhra Pradesh border-district adjacency requires one official statewide political map; the printed district table remains a dated unscored snapshot.
Andhra Pradesh totals for revenue divisions, mandals, villages, panchayats, towns and urban local bodies require one current statewide government directory and remain unscored.
The exact current composition of the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Council is time-sensitive and remains unscored pending an official current roster.
